hints: Write Newton's second law for both hanging particles: $1.3g - T = 1.3a$ for the descending mass and $T - 0.7g = 0.7a$ for the ascending mass.
Add the two equations to eliminate $T$ and find common acceleration $a$: $(1.3 - 0.7)g = (1.3 + 0.7)a$.
Substitute the acceleration back into either equation to calculate tension $T$.
walkthrough:
Write Newton's second law for each particle before the heavier mass hits the plane:
$$1.3g - T = 1.3a$$
$$T - 0.7g = 0.7a$$

Add the two equations to eliminate tension $T$ and solve for acceleration $a$:
$$(1.3 - 0.7)g = (1.3 + 0.7)a \implies 0.6(10) = 2.0a \implies 6 = 2a \implies a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Substitute $a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$ into the equation for the $0.7\text{ kg}$ particle to find $T$:
$$T = 0.7g + 0.7a = 0.7(10) + 0.7(3) = 7 + 2.1 = 9.1\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Apply Newton's second law ($F_{\text{net}} = ma$) to each particle connected by the light inextensible string passing over the smooth pulley.

For the descending particle of mass $m_1 = 1.3\text{ kg}$, downward weight is $1.3g = 13\text{ N}$ and upward tension is $T$:
$$1.3g - T = 1.3a$$
$$13 - T = 1.3a$$

For the ascending particle of mass $m_2 = 0.7\text{ kg}$, upward tension is $T$ and downward weight is $0.7g = 7\text{ N}$:
$$T - 0.7g = 0.7a$$
$$T - 7 = 0.7a$$

Add the two equations together to cancel $T$ and find the acceleration $a$:
$$(13 - T) + (T - 7) = 1.3a + 0.7a$$
$$6 = 2.0a$$
$$a = \frac{6}{2.0} = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

hints: Use the acceleration $a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$ found in part (i)(a).
The $1.3\text{ kg}$ particle starts from rest ($u = 0$) and falls through a distance of $s = 2\text{ m}$.
Use the SUVAT relation $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ to solve for time $t$.
walkthrough:
Apply the displacement equation $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $u = 0$, $s = 2\text{ m}$, and $a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$2 = 0 + \frac{1}{2}(3)t^2 = 1.5t^2$$
teacher_walkthrough: The $1.3\text{ kg}$ particle is released from rest ($u = 0$) at a height of $s = 2\text{ m}$ above the plane, moving with uniform acceleration $a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

The formula relating displacement, initial velocity, acceleration, and time is:
$$s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$$

Substitute the values $s = 2\text{ m}$, $u = 0$, and $a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$2 = 0(t) + \frac{1}{2}(3)t^2$$
$$2 = 1.5t^2$$

Divide both sides by $1.5 = \frac{3}{2}$ to isolate $t^2$:
$$t^2 = \frac{2}{1.5} = \frac{4}{3}$$

Take the positive square root to find $t$:
$$t = \sqrt{\frac{4}{3}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 1.1547\text{ s} \approx 1.15\text{ s}$$

hints: Find the speed $v$ of both particles when the $1.3\text{ kg}$ mass hits the plane after falling $2\text{ m}$ using $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$.
At this moment, the $0.7\text{ kg}$ particle has risen $2\text{ m}$ and is now at a height of $2 + 2 = 4\text{ m}$ above the plane.
After the $1.3\text{ kg}$ mass hits the plane, the string becomes slack and the $0.7\text{ kg}$ particle moves freely under gravity ($a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$).
Calculate the additional height $h_2$ reached before coming to rest using $v_f^2 = v^2 - 2gh_2$, then find the total height above the plane.
walkthrough:
Calculate the speed of the particles when the $1.3\text{ kg}$ mass hits the plane:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as = 0 + 2(3)(2) = 12 \implies v = \sqrt{12}\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Note the position of the $0.7\text{ kg}$ particle: having started $2\text{ m}$ above the plane and ascended $2\text{ m}$, it is at height $4\text{ m}$ when the string becomes slack.

Calculate the additional height $h_2$ gained by the $0.7\text{ kg}$ particle while moving freely under gravity ($a = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$):
$$0 = v^2 - 2gh_2 \implies 0 = 12 - 2(10)h_2 \implies 20h_2 = 12 \implies h_2 = \frac{12}{20} = 0.6\text{ m}$$

Sum the heights to find the greatest height above the plane:
$$h_{\text{total}} = 2 + 2 + 0.6 = 4.6\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough: The motion of the $0.7\text{ kg}$ particle occurs in two distinct stages. In Stage 1, it accelerates upward while the string is taut. In Stage 2, after the $1.3\text{ kg}$ mass hits the plane, the string goes slack and the particle moves freely under gravity.

For Stage 1, find the square of the speed $v$ when the $1.3\text{ kg}$ mass hits the plane after travelling $s = 2\text{ m}$ with acceleration $a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as = 0 + 2(3)(2) = 12$$
$$v = \sqrt{12} \approx 3.464\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

At the end of Stage 1, the $0.7\text{ kg}$ particle has risen $2\text{ m}$ from its initial height of $2\text{ m}$, so its height above the plane is:
$$h_1 = 2 + 2 = 4\text{ m}$$
For Stage 2, the string is slack, so the particle moves under gravity alone with downward acceleration $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$. At its highest point, its upward velocity is zero ($v_f = 0$).

Use the SUVAT relation $v_f^2 = v^2 - 2gh_2$ to find the additional height $h_2$:
$$0 = 12 - 2(10)h_2$$
$$0 = 12 - 20h_2$$
$$20h_2 = 12 \implies h_2 = \frac{12}{20} = 0.6\text{ m}$$

Add the initial height, the first stage rise, and the free-flight rise to find the greatest height above the plane:
$$h_{\text{greatest}} = 2 + 2 + 0.6 = 4.6\text{ m}$$
